newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise on auction, BOJ operation.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise on auction, BOJ operation.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures gained ground on Tuesday as the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s accomodative money market stance dampened fears of higher interest rates, dealers said.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's denial of a Monday news report saying he hinted at further consumption tax hikes after the scheduled rise on April 1, also boosted the market, they said.

"We saw a big rally off the open. December Euroyen gained seven to eight ticks and then settled around 98.97 for the day. The market is forecasting rates will be put up by 50 basis points during the year," said a dealer at a European house.
He said the market remained concerned about the BOJ's policy on short-term rates despite the central bank's inaction on Tuesday, which was widely viewed as accomodative.
"There were people hoping they would add 100 billion yen today. They're clearly sanctioning higher rates by allowing the unsecured call rate to trade above 0.50 percent," he said.
But he said the positive response to the Ministry of Finance's 10-year bond auction underpinned JGB and Euroyen markets.
December Euroyen was quoted at 98.97 at 1135 GMT after hitting a high of 98.99 against its IMM close at 98.91. Volume was 12,640 lots.
June JGBs settled at 125.37 against their previous 125.09.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly firmer in thin trade as players awaited the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which is expected to result in a 25-basis-point rate hike.
"I don't think there'll be a massive rally should the Fed do nothing. People will simply expect it the next time," the dealer said.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.090 against their IMM close at 94.070 on volume of 10,070 lots. September was at 93.850 against 93.830 on 6,530 lots.
